In this filing, we are proposing an overall rate change of -1.9%.  The actuarial exhibits and this memorandum will
provide support for the proposed rate change.
Credibility
The amount of credibility for each coverage indication is determined by the square root of the ultimate claim
count in the experience period divided by the standard below.
The credibility standards vary by coverage as shown in the following table.  A classical credibility method is used
to determine the claim frequency in which there is a 95% probability that the standard is within 7.5% of the actual
underlying frequency. This is then multiplied by a factor that measures the variance of the underlying distribution
of claim costs.
Coverage Standard
Bodily Injury 1876
Property Damage 1735
Uninsured Motorists Bodily Injury 2097
Uninsured Motorists Property Damage 1882
Comprehensive 3876
Collision 1613
Medical Payments 2536
Personal Injury Protection 1330
The complement of credibility for the coverage indications is based on the future net trend and is adjusted to
reflect the time period from the last rate change to the effective date of the proposed rates. This time period can
be capped if significant time has passed since the last rate change.
The formula is:
(1 +  Future Net Trend)^(Years between current approved rates and proposed effective date)
Rate Level Adjustment Factor
The methodology to calculate the Rate Level Adjustment Factors is similar to the parallelogram method described
in the "Basic Ratemaking" paper by Geoff Werner and Claudine Modlin.  The difference is instead of assuming a
uniform earning of the premium, we use the actual proportion of earned premium associated with each of the
various rate levels.
Premium Trend
The premium trend factor is comprised of a historical trend factor and future trend factor. The historical trend
period is from the midpoint of each quarter in the experience period to the midpoint of the most recent quarter.
The future trend period is from the midpoint of the current quarter to the midpoint of the proposed effective
period.
